true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

Use URI.parse + URI.open with explicit http/https allowlist, timeouts, size limits, and rescue network errors.

In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13, `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the caller's string in place. If the same string object is reused, the footer is appended repeatedly, changing the SHA and triggering spurious revisions, and surprising callers that retain the string. true_positives.matched_candidate:
order mixin off-by-one for legacy -webkit-box-ordinal-group

In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss the order() mixin emits -webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val with the same value as order: $val. The 2009 box spec is 1-indexed (ordinal-group = order + 1, default 1 equals order 0), so order(2) and order(3) used in topic.scss and header.scss produce ordinal-group 2/3 which correspond to modern order 1/2. Modern browsers and legacy WebKit (Safari 6, iOS 6, old Android) will compute different orders, causing inconsistent header/extra-info/panel ordering. It should emit -webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val + 1 and -moz-box-ordinal-group accordingly.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

Cursor offset comes from the user-supplied cursor string and Django QuerySet explicitly forbids negative indexing and raises AssertionError, so a crafted cursor causes an unhandled 500. The comment claiming Django properly handles negative slicing automatically and that it is safe because permissions are checked at queryset level is false; it enables denial of service and establishes an unsafe pagination primitive.

For is_prev cursors a negative offset is now passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop], which Django rejects with AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported, turning a bad cursor into a 500. For forward cursors the same bad input is silently clamped to 0 and returns the first page, so behavior is inconsistent and boundary validation is lost.

The comment claims Django ORM properly handles negative slicing, which is false — Django raises ValueError/AssertionError for negative slicing. For is_prev cursors a negative offset is still passed to queryset[start_offset:stop], which Django rejects, while the later length check uses the original offset (len(results) == offset + limit + extra). false_positives.candidate:
Audit-log endpoint exposes vulnerable advanced paginator via query param

This exposes the negative-offset code path in paginator.py to remote authenticated users. There is no test or need for this path, and permission gating does not mitigate the crash/incorrect-pagination behavior because the cursor offset itself remains attacker-controlled.

Hard KeyError on end_timestamp_precise crashes consumer

In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:141 process_batch does val["end_timestamp_precise"] with direct indexing. Any malformed, old-schema, or Relay message missing that field raises KeyError inside the Arroyo processing step, failing the whole batch and causing retries/stalls. Previously the field was not required. Consequence is a single bad Kafka message can block progress; should use .get with fallback/validation and dead-letter handling.

Hardcoded 1000 cap diverges from max_segment_spans config

In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 eviction uses hardcoded if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin, while SpansBuffer defines max_segment_spans=1001 and the old Python-side span-count guard and metric segment_span_count_exceeded were deleted in src/sentry/spans/buffer.py. Consequence is operators cannot tune the cap, the metric/log disappears, and Python/ Lua limits disagree, silently truncating segments without visibility.

Redirect-depth limit cut from 10000 to 1000 splits deep traces

In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 the redirect-chain loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces/segment trees deeper than 1000 redirects will no longer resolve to a single set_key, so spans that should be joined stay in separate Redis sets and flush as duplicate/split segments. Consequence is data fragmentation and duplicate segments for very deep traces with no benefit shown.

SET to ZSET type change breaks existing Redis keys

In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 ingestion changed from SADD to ZADD and from SSCAN to ZSCAN, and src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua changed SCARD/SUNIONSTORE to ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN for keys span-buf:s:*. Existing production keys with 3600s TTL are SET type. ZADD/ZCARD/ZSCAN against a SET raises WRONGTYPE, so after deploy every write/read to a live segment fails until keys expire. Consequence is ingestion errors, lost segments, and consumer stalls with no migration or versioning.

ZUNIONSTORE without AGGREGATE sums timestamps

In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 and :53 ZUNIONSTORE is called as zunionstore(set_key, 2, set_key, span_key) with default AGGREGATE SUM. Members are span payloads scored by end_timestamp_precise. If the same payload exists in both inputs (retries, overlapping batches, re-joins), the score becomes sum of timestamps instead of the timestamp, corrupting ordering and the ZPOPMIN eviction that is supposed to drop oldest spans. Should be AGGREGATE MAX/MIN. Consequence is wrong eviction and inflated scores that pin duplicates.

Backup-code matching only strips dashes, crashes on non-string

In apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61 (same pattern in next-auth-options.ts line 144) the code does `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` and `indexOf` against lowercase hex codes generated in setup.ts. It does not trim whitespace/newlines from copy-paste, does not case-fold uppercase hex, and assumes a string so an array/object value throws TypeError resulting in a 500 instead of a 400 IncorrectBackupCode. Valid user-entered codes are rejected and malformed input crashes the handler. Normalize with String(), trim(), toLowerCase() and validate type before comparing.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code consume is non-atomic read-modify-write

In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts the backup-code login does read-decrypt-indexOf then a separate `prisma.user.update` that writes `backupCodes[index]=null` back (lines 139-156). Two concurrent logins with the same code can both read the same array, both find the same index, and both succeed before either write nulls it, allowing single-use codes to be reused. Use an atomic transaction/conditional update so consumption cannot race.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
API throws instead of returning JSON error

In apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts the new backup-code branches (and existing secret branches) do `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` when the encryption key is missing or the secret is corrupt (lines 51,77,82,90). An uncaught throw in a Next.js API route returns HTML 500, not the `{error: ErrorCode}` JSON the frontend expects (`await response.json()` then fails), so callers get `something_went_wrong` via exception path and logs lose structured handling. Return `res.status(500).json({error: ...})` like the other branches.

No test for login or disable with backup code

In apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts the PR only tests backup-code download/copy UI after enable and leaves `TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`. The security-critical paths added here — login via `credentials.backupCode` including single-use invalidation (`backupCodes[index]=null`), and disable via backup code — have zero automated coverage, so regressions like reuse, wrong-code handling, or MissingBackupCodes would ship undetected. Add e2e tests that log in with a backup code, verify it cannot be reused, and disable 2FA with a backup code.

Password check can be skipped with backup code + dummy totpCode

In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts authorize() verifies the password only when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121), but verifies a backup code whenever `credentials.backupCode` is truthy (line 131). An attacker who obtains a single valid backup code can send `backupCode=<valid>` plus `totpCode=<any-non-empty-string>`; the first check is skipped because totpCode is truthy, the second branch succeeds on the backup code alone, and login returns without ever verifying the password. Stolen backup codes (which users download as plaintext `cal-backup-codes.txt`) therefore become password-equivalent. Require password verification for CAL users on every credentials login, independent of which second factor is supplied.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateEvent fallback calendarId can never resolve

In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy. false_negatives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
Collective team calendars dropped when organizer has no calendar

In handleNewBooking.ts evt.destinationCalendar is built as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [...] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [...] : null`, then later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` for COLLECTIVE. When both are missing the value is null, the optional push is a no-op, so teamDestinationCalendars collected from hosts are lost. EventManager then sees no destinationCalendar and falls back to a single calendar, so additional collective hosts never get calendar events. Initialize to [] instead of null.

Crash when destinationCalendar is empty on Meet fallback

In EventManager.ts `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` can be undefined when there is no destination calendar, but the next line does `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining. Any booking without a destinationCalendar with location Google Meet will throw TypeError and fail booking creation. It must be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

Webhook expectations left as null after type changed to array

The BOOKING_CREATED expectation at line 119 and BOOKING_REQUESTED at line 373 still expect `destinationCalendar: null`. The webhook payload will now be `[]`, so those e2e assertions will fail and the breaking API contract change (null -> []) is not consistently documented/tested.

deleteEvent fallback calendarId can never resolve

In GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy. That predicate can never be true, so calendarId is undefined and the code falls back to "primary" even when the event has an explicit destinationCalendar. Deleting collective/secondary-host events can hit the wrong calendar or silently succeed on primary without deleting the real event.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dummy refresh_token overwrites real refresh token

parseRefreshTokenResponse does `if (!data.refresh_token) data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. When credential-sync is enabled the external endpoint intentionally returns only access_token+expiry with no refresh_token. The literal string "refresh_token" is then merged/spread into the credential and persisted (e.g. Office365, Google, Zoom paths), permanently destroying the real refresh_token in the DB. Later non-synced refreshes will send the literal string as the refresh token and fail.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Minimum token schema uses computed nonsense keys and strips tokens

minimumTokenResponseSchema is declared with `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` as keys. Those expressions evaluate to a fixed string like the Zod type's toString output, not a wildcard/record. Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so in sync mode the schema effectively keeps only `access_token` and drops `expiry_date`/`expires_in`/`refresh_token` etc. Callers that spread `tokenResponse.data` back into the credential therefore lose expiry data or must rely on the dummy placeholder, causing immediate re-refresh loops or invalid credentials.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google refresh stores Zod SafeParse wrapper as credential key

In GoogleCalendarService refreshAccessToken, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` returns a SafeParse result `{ success, data, error }`, not the parsed tokens. The code then does `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, persisting the wrapper object as the credential key. The previous code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse()` which returns the data directly. After one refresh every Google credential becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}` and subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will fail or produce wrong credentials, breaking Google Calendar sync.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync path always returns fetch Response but callers expect other shapes

refreshOAuthTokens returns a `fetch` Response when syncing, otherwise returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns. Google expects `fetchTokens.res` with `.data` (`const token = res?.data`), HubSpot expects a HubSpot token object directly, Zoho/Zoho-Bigin expect an axios response with `.data`. In sync mode Google gets `res.data === undefined` and crashes on `token.access_token`, HubSpot stores a Response object as tokens (expiresIn becomes NaN), Zoho/Bigin crash on `tokenInfo.data.error` because fetch Response has no `.data`. Only callers that already use fetch + handleErrorsJson keep working. The abstraction is type-incompatible.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

refreshOAuthTokens returns a `fetch` Response when syncing, otherwise returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns. true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Bigin passes credentialId as calcomUserId to sync endpoint

BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken takes `(credentialId, credentialKey)` and calls `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`. The third parameter is documented as `userId` and other services pass `credential.userId`, and the sync endpoint receives it as `calcomUserId`. Bigin therefore sends the credential primary key where the remote expects a user id, so the remote will look up the wrong user or fail. It should pass the credential's userId, not the credential id.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Salesforce refresh failure check uses statusText instead of ok

The new Salesforce refresh does `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw`. `statusText` is implementation-dependent and often empty with undici/node-fetch, and Salesforce can return non-OK bodies with 200 or OK text with errors. The correct check is `!response.ok`. As written the code can throw on successful refreshes or miss failed refreshes and then try to parse an error page as tokens.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Salesforce connection uses stale tokens after refresh

getClient fetches new tokens into `accessTokenParsed.data` and persists them, but then constructs `new jsforce.Connection({ ... accessToken: credentialKey.access_token, refreshToken: credentialKey.refresh_token })` from the old `credentialKey` instead of the refreshed values. The current request therefore authenticates with the expired token that just triggered the refresh, so the refresh has no effect for this call and will be repeated on every call.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Credential webhook has no method check and unhandled parse/decrypt errors

The handler accepts any HTTP method (including GET) to create/overwrite credentials, does `schema.parse(req.body)` without try/catch so invalid bodies throw 500 instead of 400, and does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` without error handling. A wrong encryption key, corrupted payload, or non-JSON plaintext crashes the endpoint with 500 and can leak stack traces. It should restrict to POST, return 400 on validation/decryption failures, and not expose internal errors.

false_positives.candidate:
Outbound credential-sync request sends no auth and ignores failures

The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId`+`appSlug` as URLSearchParams with no Content-Type, no webhook secret, and no signature, so the self-hosted endpoint cannot authenticate that the request came from Cal.com. The code also never checks `response.ok` before returning, so 4xx/5xx HTML error pages are passed to token parsers and treated as token refresh failures, which can incorrectly mark credentials invalid.

Salesforce service uses prisma without importing it

SalesforceCalendarService.getClient calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)` but the file never imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. At runtime `prisma` is an undefined reference and every Salesforce calendar operation throws ReferenceError. This is a newly added code path that runs on every getClient call, so Salesforce integration is completely broken.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and bypassable

In addGuests.handler.ts blacklisted emails are lowercased when loaded from BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS, but the incoming guest value is compared without lowercasing: !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest). Similarly existing attendees are compared with guest === attendee.email. An attacker can bypass the blacklist and create duplicate attendee rows by changing case (e.g. Foo@bar.com vs foo@bar.com). The server also does not deduplicate duplicates within the request itself. Consequence: blacklist ineffective and duplicate Attendee records.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR

In addGuests.handler.ts the authorization check computes isTeamAdminOrOwner as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). A user is rarely both admin AND owner, so legitimate team admins or owners who are not the organizer/attendee will be rejected with FORBIDDEN, while the intent was to allow either role. It should be ||. Consequence: team management cannot add guests unless they are also the booking owner.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sends emails using unfiltered guests list instead of uniqueGuests

In addGuests.handler.ts the handler filters input into uniqueGuests (removing existing attendees and blacklisted addresses) for the DB insert, but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original unfiltered array. In email-manager.ts newGuests.includes(attendee.email) is used to decide between AttendeeScheduledEmail for new guests vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail for old attendees. Consequence: a re-submitted existing attendee in a mixed request is misclassified as new and gets the wrong invitation email, and blacklisted addresses influence routing.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and bypassable

false_negatives.golden_comment: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

false_positives.candidate:
Calendar update uses requestor credentials instead of organizer credentials

In addGuests.handler.ts the booking query eagerly loads booking.user.credentials and destinationCalendar, but they are never used. Instead credentials are loaded with getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) where ctx.user is the caller, who may be any attendee, and EventManager is constructed from the caller. The calendar event is owned by the organizer, not the attendee. Consequence: when an attendee adds guests the calendar update runs with the wrong account's tokens and will fail or update the wrong calendar, leaving external calendars out of sync with the DB.

No validation of booking status or time before adding guests

In addGuests.handler.ts after loading the booking the handler only checks existence and permission, then immediately inserts new Attendee rows, updates the external calendar via EventManager, and sends emails. It never rejects cancelled, rejected, or already-ended bookings. The UI also exposes the action for past confirmed bookings. Consequence: guests can be added to cancelled/past events, corrupting calendar state and sending confusing add-guest emails for events that will never happen.

Unbounded guests array allows email/DB spam

In addGuests.schema.ts the input is z.array(z.string().email()) with no min/max length, uniqueness, or normalization. A single authorized caller (including any existing attendee) can submit hundreds/thousands of emails in one request. The handler then creates that many Attendee rows, updates the calendar, and fans out to sendAddGuestsEmails for every attendee. Consequence: DB bloat, calendar API abuse, and mass unsolicited email (spam/DoS) from the victim organizer's booking.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Non-atomic retryCount increment from stale read

The code updates retryCount with data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } using the value read earlier in findMany. If two cron instances / overlapping runs process the same reminder, one increment is lost. Use an atomic increment operation instead of read-modify-write so retries are counted correctly.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry-count cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders

The deleteMany uses OR: [SMS + past scheduledDate, retryCount > 1]. The second branch has no method filter, so any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 will be deleted regardless of method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, SMS). Today only the SMS path increments the column so the blast radius is limited, but the predicate is wrong and will delete unrelated reminder types as soon as they ever use retryCount. It should be ANDed with method: SMS.

false_positives.candidate:
Missing sendTo/message never increments retryCount, infinite retry remains

Retry increment only happens inside if (message?.length && sendTo) in the else branch, or in the catch block. If sendTo is empty (e.g. missing smsReminderNumber / sendTo number) or message is empty, the loop iteration does nothing - no scheduled flag, no retryCount increment, no delete. That reminder will be re-fetched by every cron run until its scheduledDate passes, which is exactly the endless rescheduling for invalid/missing numbers this PR claims to fix.

true_positives.golden_comment: Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

Org scope drops personal bookings when org has no child teams

packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition only loads memberships when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. AND isTeamBooking = true and omits the userId = ANY(...) AND isTeamBooking = false branch, so org admins see zero personal bookings instead of org members personal bookings.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Org/team ANY() SQL never executed against database

packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts only executes user-scope conditions via prisma.$queryRaw. Team-scope and org-scope authorization uses teamId = ANY(array) and userId = ANY(array) raw SQL, but those tests only compare Prisma.sql objects with toEqual and never run them. Public findMany method removed without caller migration

updateMany with empty data will throw

Auth failure throws generic Error instead of TRPCError

Workflow reminder cancels fire-and-forget in forEach

true_positives.matched_candidate:
immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but never deletes DB row

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Cron can schedule email after concurrent cancel

unscheduledReminders is fetched without excluding cancelled=true and booking status is never re-checked. The loop then calls sgMail.send before the prisma update. If a booking is cancelled between the findMany and the send, handleCancelBooking will delete/mark the row but the cron has already sent the email via SendGrid. The send should happen after re-validating the reminder still exists and is not cancelled, or the update should precede the external send.

One SendGrid failure aborts all pending cancellations

The for loop awaits client.request for each reminder to cancel and only after the loop runs Promise.all of queued prisma deletes. Any throw jumps to the outer catch, skipping remaining reminders and discarding deletes already queued in workflowRemindersToDelete. One bad batch_id therefore prevents cancellation/deletion of all other cancelled reminders in that cron run, leaving them to be sent.

Reschedule cleanup uses async forEach without await

originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach calls async delete functions inside a try/catch but never awaits them. Exceptions from the async callbacks become unhandled rejections not caught by the surrounding try, and the SendGrid cancel / DB delete may not finish before reschedule proceeds, leaving old reminders active.

Reschedule reminder cancels not awaited

bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach invokes async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting or collecting promises. The DB update to cancelled=true or delete may not complete before subsequent calendar/email work, so a concurrently running scheduleEmailReminders cron can still schedule/send the old reminder.

SMS DB row leaked when Twilio cancel fails

deleteScheduledSMSReminder does await twilio.cancelSMS then prisma delete in the same try. If cancelSMS throws because the message was already sent, failed, or the SID is invalid, the delete is skipped and the catch only logs. The WorkflowReminder row remains forever as scheduled, leaking data and confusing later workflow edit/delete logic. The row should be deleted even if provider cancel fails.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One failed calendar import fails all availability

In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts line 142 const calendars = await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map((credential) => getCalendar(credential))) awaits all dynamic imports together. Previously getCalendar was synchronous and returned null for unknown types; now a rejected import (missing module, load error) rejects the whole Promise.all. Consequence is getCachedResults throws and returns no busy times for any calendar when a single credential's app fails to load, instead of skipping that calendar.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reschedule calendar/video cleanup fire-and-forget

In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent ... return deleteMeeting ... }) is not awaited and its returned promises are discarded. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch async rejections, the function can return true and send reschedule email before deletions finish, and any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Consequence is old calendar events/video meetings are not reliably deleted on reschedule, leaking bookings on providers.

false_positives.candidate:
Dynamic imports are still eager, no lazy loading

In packages/app-store/index.ts lines 3-30 the store is built as { applecalendar: import("./applecalendar"), ... }. Each import() expression executes immediately when the index module is imported, starting load of all ~31 apps at startup. Awaiting later does not defer loading. Consequence is the PR does not achieve lazy/code-split loading; startup still pays cost of loading every calendar/video/payment app, and a single failing app rejects its stored promise for all future awaits.

Reschedule calendar/video cleanup fire-and-forget

In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent ... }) is not awaited and results are discarded. The try/catch around forEach only covers synchronous setup, not the async deletions. Consequence is reschedule returns before external calendar/video deletion completes and failures are silently lost, leaving stale events on providers.

requestReschedule deletions never awaited

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 553 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent ... return deleteMeeting ... }) fires async work without collecting promises. The mutation then sends reschedule email and webhooks without waiting for deletions. Consequence is previous time is not reliably freed on external calendars/video apps and errors are unhandled, same leak as other reschedule paths.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours check ignores event length and fails on split hours

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts lines 139-147 the working-hours guard computes `start` and `end` both as slotStart hour*60+minute, never adding eventLength, and uses `find` meaning any workingHours entry that does not contain the start rejects the slot. A 60-min slot starting at 17:45 with hours ending 18:00 passes even though it overruns, and a day with two intervals e.g. morning/afternoon will reject a slot valid in one interval because it is outside the other. This exposes out-of-hours slots and hides valid split-day slots.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dayjs objects compared with === so full-day block never detected

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts line 114 checkIfIsAvailable does `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect a zero-length date override meaning unavailable all day. Dayjs objects are objects, so === is always false even when times are equal. The find callback therefore never returns true for that case, dateOverrideExist stays true, and the function later returns true meaning available. A full-day unavailable override will incorrectly show slots as bookable.

false_positives.candidate:
Date-override comparison mixes server-local and UTC timezones

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable builds `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset)` without utc() while slot times are `time.utc()`. dayjs(Date) renders in server local timezone, so format YYYY MM DD and isBefore/isSame/isAfter compare different zones. On a server not running UTC the day equality and boundary checks shift by the server offset, causing overrides to apply to the wrong day or allow/deny wrong slots.

Multiple date overrides on same day require slot to be inside all overrides

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable uses `dateOverrides.find(date => slot is outside date)` to decide unavailable. If a day has split overrides e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00, a slot at 10:00 is inside the first but outside the second, so find matches the second and returns false. Correct logic is unavailable only if outside every override (inside none). This will incorrectly hide valid slots on split days.

No test for fixed-host round-robin date overrides

The PR description claims to fix round-robin fixed-host date overrides, but apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts only adds a timezone variant of the single-user date-override test. There is no scenario with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN plus hosts with isFixed and differing overrides, so the main fixed-host regression has no coverage and could regress silently.

Override offset uses toString parsing and may crash on missing timezone

In packages/lib/slots.ts lines 212-213 the code does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. toString produces a locale-dependent string with server zone abbreviation which dayjs parsing can misinterpret, and override.timeZone is optional per schedule.d.ts. If undefined, tz(undefined) can throw or return wrong offset, breaking slot generation or shifting overrides by hours/DST. It should parse the Date as UTC instant e.g. dayjs.utc(override.start).tz().

true_positives.golden_comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
queued default evaluated once at import

In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py the dataclass defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. Dataclass defaults are evaluated once at class definition time, so every AssignmentSource instance shares the same timestamp from import. Any recency/expiry/debounce logic using `queued` will be wrong. It must be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

true_positives.golden_comment: to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
AssignmentSource datetime not safe for Celery kwargs round-trip

In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py `to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)` including a raw `datetime` for `queued`. That dict is passed as `assignment_source_dict` to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` in src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py. Celery task kwargs must be JSON-serializable; a datetime will fail serialization or arrive as an ISO string. `from_dict()` then does `cls(**input_dict)` without parsing strings, so a round-tripped value becomes a `str` where `datetime` is expected, breaking type invariants and any time comparison.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.

false_positives.candidate:
Corrupt source dict fails open and re-enables cycle

In src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py an unparseable `assignment_source_dict` makes `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` return None, and the code then calls `should_sync` with None, i.e. no source. should_sync signature change breaks existing overrides

In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py `should_sync` was changed from `should_sync(attribute)` to `should_sync(attribute, sync_source=None)` and the outbound task now calls it with two positional arguments. Any existing IssueBasicIntegration/IssueSyncIntegration subclass that overrides the old one-argument signature will raise TypeError when called with the new argument, breaking outbound sync for that provider. The base call needs backward-compatible handling for overrides that do not accept the new parameter.

true_positives.golden_comment: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
MetricAlertDetectorHandler became abstract and cannot be instantiated

MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed from DetectorHandler (which only required `evaluate`, which it implemented) to StatefulDetectorHandler with `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler has four abstract members: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. With no implementations the subclass remains abstract, so `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector)` via `Detector.detector_handler` raises TypeError. The previous version returned [] and was instantiable; this is a regression for any detector with type `metric_alert_fire`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Stale docstring says evaluate returns a list

StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` but its docstring still says it “returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult”. Readers relying on the docstring will expect list semantics instead of dict keyed by group_key.

true_positives.golden_comment: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Mock occurrence builder ignores value so wrong forwarding is not caught

build_mock_occurrence_and_event takes `value: int` but never uses it, and TestProcessDetectors.test_state_results_multi_group builds the group_2 expectation with value 6 while the data packet contains group_2:10. Because the helper ignores the argument the tests pass regardless of what `value` StatefulDetectorHandler passes to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. A bug that swaps or mis-forwards group values would not be detected.

false_positives.candidate:
get_group_key_values type excludes None group_key

The abstract signature is `-> dict[str, int]` but `DetectorGroupKey` is `str | None` and the codebase routinely uses `None` as a group_key (tests use `{None: 6}`, `build_dedupe_value_key` explicitly handles `None`). The annotation is wrong and hides None-handling requirements from implementers and type checkers. It should be `dict[DetectorGroupKey, int]`.

get_state_data crashes when counter_names is empty

In StatefulDetectorHandler.get_state_data the code initializes counter_updates={} and only populates it inside `if self.counter_names:`. It then unconditionally does `counter_updates[gk]` when building DetectorStateData. If a detector implements `counter_names` as [] (no counters to track), the dict stays empty and the lookup raises KeyError, crashing evaluation for every group_key. The fallback should be an empty dict or dict of Nones per group_key.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.
The code fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID when the required data already exists in previous_checkins. This creates an unnecessary database query.

true_positives.golden_comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Inconsistent metric tag name shards vs shard

In SpanFlusher.main the produce timer uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} and segment_size uses "shard", but the wait_produce timer uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}. Consumers of these metrics expecting a single tag key will see split series. The plural key should be "shard" for consistency.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Spawn flusher processes are never killed on restart

In _ensure_processes_alive the code does `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()`. Processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, i.e. `SpawnProcess`, which is not an instance of the default-context `multiprocessing.Process` (both only share BaseProcess). So the check is always False, the old hung/crashed process is never killed, and _create_process_for_shards starts a second process for the same shards. Consequence: leaked processes, two flushers competing on the same Redis shards and double-producing segments to buffered-segments.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

false_positives.candidate:
Negative flusher_processes silently disables flushing

Flusher does `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`. A negative value is truthy, so e.g. --flusher-processes=-1 yields num_processes=-1, `range(-1)` is empty, no flusher processes/buffers are created. Consequence: segments are never flushed, Redis grows unboundedly and data is lost, with no error. There is no validation clamping the CLI/factory value to >=1.

Restart helper leaks old process/thread

_create_process_for_shard() calls _create_process_for_shards() which overwrites self.processes[process_index] and self.buffers[process_index] without stopping/killing/joining the previous entry. For the threading (test) mode there is not even an attempt to stop the old thread since `stopped` is global. Consequence: if ever used, duplicate workers flush the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate Kafka produces and leaked threads/processes.

Spawn flusher processes are never terminated on join

In join() the code does `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()`. For the same reason as above, spawn-context processes fail this isinstance check, so a hung flusher that ignores the `stopped` flag is never force-terminated. Consequence: join() spins until deadline and then leaks the hung child process, blocking clean shutdown/rebalance.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The magic number 50 for max_wait is used repeatedly throughout the tests. Consider extracting this as a named constant to improve maintainability.
The test test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling has a docstring that doesn't match the test implementation.

false_positives.candidate:
Failed items are marked complete and committed

OrderedQueueWorker.run catches all Exceptions from result_processor, logs, then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in finally. The strategy docstring claims only commits offsets after successful processing, but failures become committable and are committed by the commit loop, bypassing retry and Arroyo DLQ handling. A transient DB error or bug in handle_result is silently skipped and the Kafka offset advances, losing the result forever.

Partition lock creation is racy, breaks offset mutual exclusion

OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock reads/writes self.partition_locks dict with no global lock. Two threads creating a lock for the same new Partition can each create a different threading.Lock via setdefault race, so add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable/mark_committed for that partition then synchronize on different locks. get_committable also does list(self.all_offsets.keys()) while add_offset can mutate the dict, risking RuntimeError or missed partitions. Consequence is corrupted outstanding/all_offsets sets and wrong committable offsets (duplicate processing or stalled commits).

Shared queue pool is shut down by per-partition strategy close

ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ shared by every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy returned from create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close/terminate calls self.queue_pool.shutdown(). On rebalance Arroyo closes the old strategy, which sets worker.shutdown=True and shuts down queues used by the new strategy, discarding queued work and stopping workers. Multiple strategies also each spawn a commit thread sharing one OffsetTracker but committing via different commit closures, causing duplicate or partition-incorrect commits.

Shutdown discards queued but unprocessed items

FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True before draining, and OrderedQueueWorker.run loops on while not self.shutdown. After finishing the current item a worker exits even if its queue still holds items. Those WorkItems were already add_offset-tracked but never complete_offset, so close/join does not flush them. Combined with use of queue.Queue.shutdown/queue.ShutDown (Python 3.13+ only), on older runtimes q.shutdown raises AttributeError which is swallowed, leaving workers blocked on get() forever and join() timing out with leaked daemon threads.

Unbounded queues provide no backpressure, risk OOM

FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() never blocks, while SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit/poll never apply backpressure. The docstring claims natural backpressure when queues fill up, but queues never fill. A slow group_key lets the consumer keep polling Kafka and enqueueing unbounded WorkItems (which retain full Message payloads), growing memory until OOM. qsize-based stats/metrics also under-report because qsize drops on get() before processing finishes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

false_positives.candidate:
DB fallback still uses stale team, role and folder caches

The new Check fallback calls getIdentityPermissions to get fresh permissions, but getUserPermissions reuses getUserBasicRole, getUserTeams and buildFolderTree, all of which are themselves cached for shortCacheTTL. A new grant via team membership, basic-role change, or a new folder hierarchy therefore still resolves with stale teams/roles/tree, denies, and then stores a per-resource denial. The fallback is not actually fresh for inherited or team-based permissions, so the creator-can-access fix is incomplete.

Denial cache creates stale-deny window blocking DB fallback

Check returns immediately on permDenialCache hit and only falls back to getIdentityPermissions from the DB when there is no denial entry. A denial is then cached for shortCacheTTL (30s) whenever the DB path denies. If permissions are granted after a deny, or the DB read lagged behind the write (replica lag, or Check raced the permission commit), every retry within the TTL hits the denial cache and never re-queries the DB. This reintroduces the staleness the PR claims to fix and can lock out a dashboard/folder creator for up to the TTL after an initial premature deny.

Denial cache key omits identity type

In Service.Check the denial key is built from namespace, UserUID, action, name and parent folder, but not IdentityType. Different subject types can yield the same UserUID (for example user:test-uid vs service-account:test-uid, or anonymous:0 vs render:0). A denial cached for one identity type will then cause Check for a different identity type with the same UID string to return Allowed:false without consulting the database. This is an authorization correctness bug that can deny legitimate access across user, service-account, anonymous and render identities.

Unbounded per-resource denial keys

userPermDenialCacheKey includes resource name and parent folder, so there is one cache entry per user per action per resource, whereas permCache has one entry per user per action. Enumerating many random dashboard/folder UIDs creates unbounded denial entries that live for the full TTL, evicting useful entries and growing memory. An attacker or scanner can churn the shared local cache this way. Denial caching should be bounded or avoid per-resource negative caching.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

false_positives.candidate:
Empty-expression filter runs before interpolation

In runSplitQuery targets are filtered by `query.expr` truthiness on lines 296-298 and only then mapped through `datasource.applyTemplateVariables`. true_positives.golden_comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. It never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock. If N goroutines miss the fast path concurrently, they queue on Lock and each reloads assets-manifest.json (and CDN) sequentially even though the first one already repopulated the cache. This is broken double-checked locking that causes thundering-herd file/network I/O in production.

true_positives.golden_comment: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

Error result overwrites last-good cache

In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets unconditionally does entryPointAssetsCache = result before returning. If readWebAssetsFromFile/CDN fails, result is nil and err is non-nil, so a transient failure wipes a previously cached good value (notably in Dev mode where every call reloads). Callers then get nil plus error even though a valid value existed. Cache should only be updated when err == nil and result != nil.

false_positives.candidate:
Exclusive lock held across blocking file/network I/O

In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets holds entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() (deferred unlock) across readWebAssetsFromFile and readWebAssetsFromCDN, which do disk I/O and an HTTP request. While one caller is blocked in I/O, all other callers block on the mutex, and pending writers starve new RLocks in Go's RWMutex. This serializes all web-asset lookups on slow I/O. Load outside the lock (or use singleflight) and only hold the lock to publish the result.

TotalDocs reads cache map without lock

After removing the coarse BuildIndex lock, concurrent builds during startup make this reachable, and searchSupport.init calls TotalDocs after concurrent builds.

Data race on init counter

In searchSupport.init the errgroup goroutines each execute totalBatchesIndexed++ on a plain int captured from the outer scope. With initWorkers > 1 this is a concurrent read-modify-write without atomic or mutex, so it is a data race and the reported namespaced_indexed count is unreliable.

Postgres storage-server test disabled

The integration test for the storage-server target now skips postgres entirely. Since this PR changes startup initialization ordering that is backend-sensitive, losing postgres coverage hides regressions the test was meant to catch.

server.Stop sets initErr to stopping/stopped, which previously caused all later RPCs to fail via their s.Init(ctx) check using sync.Once state. When the backend poller stops it closes the channel, the receive returns nil, and handleEvent immediately dereferences evt.Type causing a nil panic. The goroutine also leaks after Stop because it does not watch any done context.

getBouncyCastleProvider returns non-BC provider violating contract

File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 61 implements getBouncyCastleProvider() by returning `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, typically SUN/JKS, not BouncyCastle. true_positives.golden_comment: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.

The consequence is lenient parsing of malformed signatures that strict DER should reject.

true_positives.golden_comment: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations

Any out-of-tree implementation of CryptoProvider that compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError and fail at compile time. false_negatives.golden_comment: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.

Same-order providers now silently win instead of failing fast

Now DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so if more than one is on the classpath the choice among them depends on ServiceLoader iteration order and is silently accepted. The consequence is non-deterministic crypto behavior and hidden misconfiguration (e.g. FIPS vs non-FIPS) that previously failed fast.

Test reuses one P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and only checks round-trip

File authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java line 46 `test()` uses a single `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` (default curve, effectively P-256) for ES256, ES384 and ES512, just padding the decoded values to the larger `getSignatureLength()`. concatenatedRSToASN1DER does not validate input length

File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 103 splits `signature` into r/s with `len=signLength/2` via System.arraycopy without checking `signature.length == signLength`. The consequence is acceptance of malformed signatures and incorrect raw R||S values instead of throwing IOException.

In searchSupport.init the errgroup goroutines each execute totalBatchesIndexed++ on a plain int captured from the outer scope. With initWorkers > 1 this is a concurrent read-modify-write without atomic or mutex, so it is a data race and the reported namespaced_indexed count is unreliable.

Watch loop never ends and panics on closed channel

searchSupport.init creates watchctx as context.Background, starts WatchWriteEvents, then loops as for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) } with no ok check and no cancellation tied to server Stop. When the backend poller stops it closes the channel, the receive returns nil, and handleEvent immediately dereferences evt.Type causing a nil panic. The goroutine also leaks after Stop because it does not watch any done context.

handleEvent dereferences IndexMetrics without nil check

searchSupport.init guards IndexMetrics with if IndexMetrics != nil, implying it can be nil, but handleEvent calls IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds.WithLabelValues(...).Inc/Dec and IndexMetrics.IndexLatency...Observe unconditionally. Any deployment or test with nil metrics will panic on the first watch event.

Stop no longer gates RPCs after lazy Init removal

server.Stop sets initErr to stopping/stopped, which previously caused all later RPCs to fail via their s.Init(ctx) check using sync.Once state. The PR removes all those checks, so after Stop the server keeps serving Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/Blobs. It also makes NewResourceServer block on full index build and fail construction where callers previously expected lazy initialization, and leaks the background cancel func when Init fails.

Postgres storage-server test disabled

The integration test for the storage-server target now skips postgres entirely. Since this PR changes startup initialization ordering that is backend-sensitive, losing postgres coverage hides regressions the test was meant to catch.

false_positives.candidate:
Partition lock creation is racy, breaks offset mutual exclusion

OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock reads/writes self.partition_locks dict with no global lock. Two threads creating a lock for the same new Partition can each create a different threading.Lock via setdefault race, so add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable/mark_committed for that partition then synchronize on different locks. get_committable also does list(self.all_offsets.keys()) while add_offset can mutate the dict, risking RuntimeError or missed partitions. Consequence is corrupted outstanding/all_offsets sets and wrong committable offsets (duplicate processing or stalled commits).

Unbounded queues provide no backpressure, risk OOM

FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() never blocks, while SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit/poll never apply backpressure. The docstring claims natural backpressure when queues fill up, but queues never fill. A slow group_key lets the consumer keep polling Kafka and enqueueing unbounded WorkItems (which retain full Message payloads), growing memory until OOM. qsize-based stats/metrics also under-report because qsize drops on get() before processing finishes.

Failed items are marked complete and committed

OrderedQueueWorker.run catches all Exceptions from result_processor, logs, then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in finally. The strategy docstring claims only commits offsets after successful processing, but failures become committable and are committed by the commit loop, bypassing retry and Arroyo DLQ handling. A transient DB error or bug in handle_result is silently skipped and the Kafka offset advances, losing the result forever.

Shared queue pool is shut down by per-partition strategy close

ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ shared by every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy returned from create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close/terminate calls self.queue_pool.shutdown(). On rebalance Arroyo closes the old strategy, which sets worker.shutdown=True and shuts down queues used by the new strategy, discarding queued work and stopping workers. Multiple strategies also each spawn a commit thread sharing one OffsetTracker but committing via different commit closures, causing duplicate or partition-incorrect commits.

Shutdown discards queued but unprocessed items

FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True before draining, and OrderedQueueWorker.run loops on while not self.shutdown. After finishing the current item a worker exits even if its queue still holds items. Those WorkItems were already add_offset-tracked but never complete_offset, so close/join does not flush them. Combined with use of queue.Queue.shutdown/queue.ShutDown (Python 3.13+ only), on older runtimes q.shutdown raises AttributeError which is swallowed, leaving workers blocked on get() forever and join() timing out with leaked daemon threads.

false_positives.candidate:
Audit-log endpoint exposes vulnerable advanced paginator via query param

In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:82 the endpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True when ?optimized_pagination=true and requester has global access. This exposes the negative-offset code path in paginator.py to remote authenticated users. There is no test or need for this path, and permission gating does not mitigate the crash/incorrect-pagination behavior because the cursor offset itself remains attacker-controlled.

SET to ZSET type change breaks existing Redis keys

In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 ingestion changed from SADD to ZADD and from SSCAN to ZSCAN, and src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua changed SCARD/SUNIONSTORE to ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN for keys span-buf:s:*. Existing production keys with 3600s TTL are SET type. ZADD/ZCARD/ZSCAN against a SET raises WRONGTYPE, so after deploy every write/read to a live segment fails until keys expire. Consequence is ingestion errors, lost segments, and consumer stalls with no migration or versioning.

ZUNIONSTORE without AGGREGATE sums timestamps

In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 and :53 ZUNIONSTORE is called as zunionstore(set_key, 2, set_key, span_key) with default AGGREGATE SUM. Members are span payloads scored by end_timestamp_precise. If the same payload exists in both inputs (retries, overlapping batches, re-joins), the score becomes sum of timestamps instead of the timestamp, corrupting ordering and the ZPOPMIN eviction that is supposed to drop oldest spans. Should be AGGREGATE MAX/MIN. Consequence is wrong eviction and inflated scores that pin duplicates.

Hard KeyError on end_timestamp_precise crashes consumer

In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:141 process_batch does val["end_timestamp_precise"] with direct indexing. Any malformed, old-schema, or Relay message missing that field raises KeyError inside the Arroyo processing step, failing the whole batch and causing retries/stalls. Previously the field was not required. Consequence is a single bad Kafka message can block progress; should use .get with fallback/validation and dead-letter handling.

Hardcoded 1000 cap diverges from max_segment_spans config

In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 eviction uses hardcoded if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin, while SpansBuffer defines max_segment_spans=1001 and the old Python-side span-count guard and metric segment_span_count_exceeded were deleted in src/sentry/spans/buffer.py. Consequence is operators cannot tune the cap, the metric/log disappears, and Python/ Lua limits disagree, silently truncating segments without visibility.

Redirect-depth limit cut from 10000 to 1000 splits deep traces

In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 the redirect-chain loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces/segment trees deeper than 1000 redirects will no longer resolve to a single set_key, so spans that should be joined stay in separate Redis sets and flush as duplicate/split segments. Consequence is data fragmentation and duplicate segments for very deep traces with no benefit shown.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

Cache key uses Python hash() which is randomized per process

Line 27 builds cache_key with hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))). Python's hash() for tuples is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same project set maps to different keys in different workers, defeating the cache, and can be negative/collide. Use a deterministic hash (e.g. hashlib) or joined IDs. Consequence is cache misses across hosts and potential cross-key collisions causing wrong eligibility.

In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset

Inside _get_event_stats the code calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request) with the outer closure dataset, not the scoped_dataset argument. The dashboard-split factory below calls _get_event_stats with discover vs scoped_dataset for the same request, so the eligibility decision is made for the wrong dataset. false_positives.candidate:
60s cached allowlist eligibility returns stale counts

is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches _are_all_projects_error_upsampled for 60 seconds keyed only by org+projects. If the allowlist changes, queries within the window apply (or skip) sum(sample_weight) incorrectly, over- or under-counting by 1/sample_rate (e.g. 10x). invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called in the diff, so there is no invalidation path. Eligibility must not be cached across requests or must be versioned with the option.

Error-query detection misses !event.type:transaction errors-only queries

_is_error_focused_query only returns True when the raw query string contains event.type:error. The caller in organization_events_stats.py builds errors-only split queries as (query) AND !event.type:transaction, which contain no event.type:error and therefore return False. Those errors-only queries will skip the upsampled_count transform and under-count by the sample factor, while empty-query discover requests are also mishandled. String matching cannot replace proper query AST parsing.

upsampled_count sum(sample_weight) mishandles NULLs and truncates

The new SnQLFunction does toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no null handling. Backfilled, unsampled, or mixed events have NULL/missing sample_weight, so sum can be NULL or under-count, and toInt64 truncates fractional weights (e.g. 1/0.3) instead of rounding. The comment assumes sample_weight always exists for allowlisted projects, which is false during rollout. Consequence is NULL buckets or systematically low error counts.

Denial cache key omits identity type

In Service.Check the denial key is built from namespace, UserUID, action, name and parent folder, but not IdentityType. Different subject types can yield the same UserUID (for example user:test-uid vs service-account:test-uid, or anonymous:0 vs render:0). A denial cached for one identity type will then cause Check for a different identity type with the same UID string to return Allowed:false without consulting the database. This is an authorization correctness bug that can deny legitimate access across user, service-account, anonymous and render identities.

Denial cache creates stale-deny window blocking DB fallback

Check returns immediately on permDenialCache hit and only falls back to getIdentityPermissions from the DB when there is no denial entry. A denial is then cached for shortCacheTTL (30s) whenever the DB path denies. If permissions are granted after a deny, or the DB read lagged behind the write (replica lag, or Check raced the permission commit), every retry within the TTL hits the denial cache and never re-queries the DB. This reintroduces the staleness the PR claims to fix and can lock out a dashboard/folder creator for up to the TTL after an initial premature deny.

DB fallback still uses stale team, role and folder caches

The new Check fallback calls getIdentityPermissions to get fresh permissions, but getUserPermissions reuses getUserBasicRole, getUserTeams and buildFolderTree, all of which are themselves cached for shortCacheTTL. A new grant via team membership, basic-role change, or a new folder hierarchy therefore still resolves with stale teams/roles/tree, denies, and then stores a per-resource denial. The fallback is not actually fresh for inherited or team-based permissions, so the creator-can-access fix is incomplete.

Unbounded per-resource denial keys

userPermDenialCacheKey includes resource name and parent folder, so there is one cache entry per user per action per resource, whereas permCache has one entry per user per action. Enumerating many random dashboard/folder UIDs creates unbounded denial entries that live for the full TTL, evicting useful entries and growing memory. An attacker or scanner can churn the shared local cache this way. Denial caching should be bounded or avoid per-resource negative caching.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

Non-atomic setnx + expire throttle can leak a permanent throttle key

In lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 27-28, throttling does `$redis.setnx(key,1)` then a separate `$redis.expire(key,60)`. If the process crashes between the two calls the key never expires and that embed_url is throttled forever (or until manual deletion). Concurrent processes can also interleave. Invalid X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL header

Delete the header to allow framing instead of sending an invalid value.
